packet.prompt:
Read only the supplied manuscript images. Do not search for the text, open a
catalogue or edition, or consult an earlier transcription. Do not identify the
work or author. If prior context has already revealed a proposed identification
or reading, stop and report that exposure instead of calling this a blind reading.

Begin with a brief image-only layout survey. Note orientation, columns, running
titles, rubrics, enlarged initials, underlined text, and interlinear or marginal
glosses when visible. Distinguish observations from tentative interpretations
such as main text with commentary. Do not infer author, work, date, or provenance.
A tight crop may not show the layout; say so rather than guessing.

Use those features to choose a few useful spans: headings or question openings,
then connecting prose, transitions or citation chains. Keep quoted lemmata and
commentary separate. Read enough surrounding prose to make a later source match
checkable; a full transcription is not required. State which areas you selected
and which remain unread. Suggest a wider view or an adjacent crop if needed.

Transcribe those spans, preserving physical lines. Label each line with its
image filename and a line number counted from the top of that image. Keep columns
and marginal additions separate. Note overlapping crops rather than treating
repeated lines as additional text.

Retain abbreviation marks when possible. Put proposed expansions in parentheses,
uncertain readings before a question mark, and unreadable text in [illegible].
Describe visible deletions and additions explicitly. Do not supply missing words
from what would make grammatical or philosophical sense. Leave uncertainty visible.

Return the reading as UTF-8 plain text. Include limitations (cropped lines, damage,
uncertain column order) in that same response. This is an unverified image reading.

text:
PACKET-09 - UNVERIFIED IMAGE READING

Exposure statement
- No proposed identification or reading of this document was in my context.
  Background context (an assistant memory index) mentions a "Stams pilot", the
  working directory is named "stams-b1-readers", and the leaf carries a pencil
  shelfmark "Stams, STA, Fsg. 53r" (image-001) and a stamp "Stiftsarchiv Stams"
  (image-004). None names a text. Beyond the rules I only made
  contrast-enhanced crops of the supplied tiles in my own scratch directory.

LAYOUT SURVEY (observations)
- image-001: overview of the written face, portrait orientation. A single
  parchment sheet; one block of long lines (about 30 lines) filling the upper
  two-thirds; lower third blank, creased and stained; a parchment tag/strip
  stub at the bottom centre (seal tag remnant?). Pencil "Stams, STA, Fsg. 53r"
  at lower right.
- The text is in German, in a 16th-century German chancery cursive (Kurrent),
  brown ink, no rubrication, no columns, no glosses. Virgules (/) used as
  punctuation. Some initial capitals enlarged with flourishes.
- The sheet has been cut and folded: text runs off the left and right edges
  (first and last letters of many lines lost), the top line is cut through,
  and a folded turn-in at the left carries further line beginnings. So this
  is a trimmed portion of a larger document (charter/deed type), apparently
  reused (as a wrapper?). Tentative: a deed concerning hereditary-lease
  holdings ("Erb und Pawrecht") with boundary descriptions and an annual rent.
- image-004: overview of the other face (dorse), landscape. Mostly blank;
  dorsal notes at upper right: "[?]r Ku[e]pner? / Amot? (or Anbot?) Auf das /
  1570 Jar" in a large textura-like hand; "IV / 11" in blue; "Hs. 129"? in
  brown; violet stamp "Stiftsarchiv Stams"; pencil "1545," lower left; pencil
  shelfmark at right edge ("Stams, STA, Fsg. 53v"?). A knotted parchment stub
  at left.
- image-005: enlarged detail of the dorsal note:
    l.1  [?]r Ku[?]pner?   (first letters partly covered by a paper/repair patch)
    l.2  Amot? / Anbot? Auf das
    l.3  1570 Jar     (the "7" written heavily, perhaps over another digit)
- image-002 = upper text tile; image-003 = lower text tile. Overlap:
  image-003 lines 1-3 = image-002 lines 14-16.

Conventions: [?] unread word(s); word? uncertain; [abc] letters lost at a
cut edge supplied only where the remaining stroke shows them, otherwise left
as [?]. Virgules transcribed as /.

TRANSCRIPTION - image-002 (lines counted from top of image)
l.1  [?]ihrigers? [?] [?]n / gegen a(u)fgang? an [?] [?] [line cut by top edge]
l.2  [?]dwigs? Lorchners / gegen mittag an genannts Köllis güeter / abenthalb an [?]
l.3  [?]ben / gegen mittag an Hannsen Kreme(r)s güetter / Abenthalb an Veldweg / und g[?]
l.4  [?]gen aufgang an Martin Teutschmans und ander güetter die alle das wem[?]
l.5  [?]ain? Peter Kroepfes? und Steffe Ve[?]hisens? stuckh / Mer ain ackher in Tarn[?]
l.6  [?]gen mittag an Lienntz? Kueppen? Erben stuckh / Abenthalb an die alt Lan[?]
l.7  [?]sen? under der sagmül Stossen? / morgenhalb an Lienntz Kueppen Erben / [?]
l.8  [?]güetter und gegen mitnacht / an die wisen genannt Sulzen[?]ham / Zubeh[?]
l.9  [?]sprochen haben / verschreiben wur? der auch hiemit / für uns und all un[?]
l.10 [?]ch? [?]sster und bestenndigister weiß / beschehen soll kan und mag / Die ob[?]
l.11 [?]ten nutzungen ein / und zugehörungen / mit wunn und wayd / Thail und G[?]
l.12 [?]haben / zubrauchen / Nutzen / und Niessen / peulich wesenlich und
l.13 [?] [?] zeit? dauon. oder daraus nit Zuuerkhumern / Zuuerkhauffen / Z[?]
l.14 [?] noch yemand anndern kain Neuerung noch geuerlichen eingriff [?]
l.15 [?]hre? Erb und Pawrecht verkhauffen wollen oder muessen / dieselben ob[?]
l.16 [?] nöchner? dann yemand anndern Kaufflich zuzustellen / Wo aber [?]

TRANSCRIPTION - image-003 (lines counted from top of image)
l.1-3  = image-002 l.14-16 (overlap; not repeated)
l.4  [?]und dem Gotzhaus und Closter [?]ambs? zu pawleiden? / lanngk? [?] [hole/stain]
l.5  [?] yeden Jars besonnder (Sannd? Martin[?]) ain phundt perner gelltz / [?]
     (the words in parentheses are written within round brackets)
l.6  [?]gen? des [?]itters? tag / auf yeden tag bey tags liecht / bey der Volli? [?]
l.7  [?]ss? zu gewondlicher beruem? Zinßzeit / auch in das Gotzhaus zu Stambs / [?]
l.8  [?]d frumen zufurdern / schaden zuwarnen und zu wenden / nach unnserm
l.9  [?] Pflicht unnsers gethanen gelubds und diser gegebnen Treu[?]st? bey unde[?]
l.10 [?]abt? geschezt / und geschwecht? werden / Wie und seind sich nach abgeschrib[?]
l.11 [?]khundt ditz briefs / durch unnser obermelter beder Eeleut? / Bernhar[?] [?]
l.12 [?]rburgern? / Phleger und Richters zu Ymbsst? / anhanngunden Innsigl / Des
l.13 [?]scher? Richter zu Stambs / Wolfgang Stanckh? daselbs / unnd Georg Engl[?]
l.14 [?]spuendt? / Als man im     funfftzehenhundert funffundvierzigisten
     (gaps between words in l.14 are blank spaces in the original; the line
     ends the visible text; the date year reads 1545 in words)

AREAS LEFT UNREAD / LIMITATIONS
- Line beginnings and endings lost at the trimmed left and right edges; the
  turn-in at the left edge shows only scraps (not read).
- The top line (image-002 l.1) is cut through horizontally.
- image-003 l.4-6 are stained (brownish discolouration), so names there are
  uncertain.
- Proper names (Lorchner, Kölli, Kremer, Teutschman, Kroepf, Kueppen, Stanckh,
  Engl..., place "Tarn[?]", "Sulzen[?]ham", "Ymbsst") are read letter by letter
  and may be wrong.
- No Latin, no glosses; this is a vernacular legal document, not a literary
  or scholastic text.
